evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/iot.tsx:78-80 — the IoT dashboard wrapper destructures only `{ data, isLoading }` from useIotDashboard(), useSensors() and useSensorReadings(); the queries' isError/error are dropped and never threaded into IotDashboardPage (its props expose dashboardLoading/sensorsLoading/readingsLoading but NO error flags).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/iot/pages/IotDashboardPage.tsx:76-96 — on a failed dashboard fetch, `dashboard` is undefined and the KPI cards render `dashboard?.total_sensors ?? 0`, `active_sensors ?? 0`, `offline_sensors ?? 0`, `unresolved_alerts ?? 0`, so a manager sees an all-zero 'healthy empty building' view that is indistinguishable from a backend/network failure — misleading state on a monitoring surface (Epic 14 FR75). Fix: destructure isError from the read queries, pass an error flag down, and render an explicit error panel instead of zeroed KPIs.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/outages.tsx:42 — `const { data, isLoading } = useOutages(queryParams);` drops isError/error; OutagesPage (UC-12 Utility Outages) receives `outages`/`total`/`isLoading` props but no error prop (OutagesPage.tsx has 0 error references).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/outages/pages/OutagesPage.tsx:72-85 — on a failed list fetch, `outages` is an empty array, so OutageList renders a normal empty state; a failed load is indistinguishable from 'no active outages' — exactly the wrong signal for a utility-outage list where empty vs. failed is safety-relevant. Fix: thread isError into the wrapper and surface a retryable error state distinct from the empty state.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/leases.tsx:587 — `const { data, isLoading } = useLeases({ organization_id: organizationId });` drops isError; `leases = (data?.items ?? [])` and `total={data?.total ?? 0}` are passed to LeasesListPage with no error prop.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/leases/pages/LeasesListPage.tsx:229 — the page renders its empty state (`!isLoading && leases.length === 0`) whenever the query fails, since a failed fetch yields `leases=[]`; the user sees 'no leases' instead of a load-failure message. Same swallowed-read-error anti-pattern as the iot and outages route-group wrappers — a shared fix (destructure isError + render a distinct error state) applies across these route groups. Fix: surface isError and render an error state separate from the empty state.
